messages:
elaine: Quick question about streaming auth: we're using a signed service-account JWT (1h exp) to exchange for an access token, but long-running streams get a 401 ~30m in and the SDK doesn't refresh. Is that expected behavior or should the SDK auto-reauth?

devex-bot: docs: https://internal.redwood.dev/streaming-auth — notes on token rotation and handlers (TLDR: SDK will call getToken/onReauth if provided).

aj: Short answer: SDK can reauth if you give it a callback to fetch a fresh token. The signed SA JWT approach is fine, but the exchange token you get back is short-lived; prefer an OIDC refresh exchange if you need the session to last arbitrarily long. Also confirm your token audience (aud) matches the streaming endpoint (e.g., https://inference.redwood.ai/stream).

sam: Repro steps I saw: create stream, wait ~25-40m, see 401, then SDK emits 'auth_error' and stream closes. No automatic retry in our older Node SDK v0.9.2.

aj: Example pattern (pseudo):
```js
const stream = new RedwoodStream({
  getToken: async () => {
    // exchange SA JWT -> access token or use OIDC refresh flow
    return await fetchAccessTokenForCurrentSubject();
  },
  onReauthError: (err) => console.warn('reauth failed', err)
});
```
Make sure getToken returns a fresh token when called; the SDK will call it before doing a reauth handshake.

ryan: Note on scopes/audience: If you're doing JWT-bearer exchange (urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer) you pass scopes in the token request body, not in the signed JWT itself. For OIDC flows, the id_token/audience needs to match the runtime. If aud mismatch, the runtime rejects.

elaine: Clarify: we also do cross-project impersonation (service A in project X calling as SA in project Y). Will impersonation break streaming reauth?

aj: It's supported but a few gotchas: the service account performing impersonation needs iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken on the target SA, and the exchanged token will be scoped to the target project. SDK treats project-scoped credentials as part of connection identity. If the token you exchange during reauth uses a different project/subject than the stream was created with, older SDKs will drop the connection because project identity changed.

sam: I hit exactly that — reauth returned a token for the impersonated SA in project-b, SDK sees project id change and terminates stream with "identity_mismatch".

aj: Two options: (1) keep the impersonation stable for the lifetime of the stream (recommended), or (2) upgrade SDK to v1.x which has an option allowProjectSwitchInStream: true (experimental) that will allow hot-swapping the project identity during reauth. There are still caveats around KV cache and telemetry attribution.

ryan: For reproducible tests, we should add an e2e that exercises: original SA -> impersonate B -> reauth returns token for B -> ensure stream stays open (or verify explicit close behavior). I'll add a test in eng-ml.

dev-marco: I'll take the SDK change/PR to add opt-in toggles for project switch. Ping me the repro + minimal test. :eyes:

elaine: Thanks — I will try switching our exchange flow to OIDC refresh (rotate refresh_token server-side) and wire getToken into the stream. Will post logs here.

aj: Also, if you rely on long-lived server sessions, consider using a short polling keepalive on the stream and a reconnect strategy that preserves conversation state (KV prefix + parent conversation id). That way a reconnect on reauth is graceful.

sam: Filed a short internal issue to track: "streaming: reauth + impersonation project-switch" (no external id here). assigning to @dev-marco.

elaine: perfect — assigning a quick follow-up ticket to devex backlog. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
